translation_notes: `graph.value(atlas_uri, owl.deprecated)` -> `m{ {atlas_uri} owl:deprecated ?v }.first()`, tested with `is None` as in the original (a present-but-falsy `owl:deprecated false` must NOT count as absent: call 2 of the driver). `(None, None, Literal(atlas_id)) in graph` -> `bool(m{ ?s ?p {Literal(atlas_id)} })` (existence; `Literal(..)` kept in the interpolation so a lang-tagged or typed literal of the same text does not match). The three `graph.add` on the shared subject -> one `+{ {atlas_uri} rdfs:seeAlso {Literal(revoked_by)} ; owl:deprecated true ; rdfs:comment {Literal(f"...{revoked_by}")} }` (the draft's `graph += g{ }` replaced), `Literal(True)` written `true`. `@graph graph` is the first line of the function.
`owl = Namespace(...)` / `rdfs = Namespace(...)` become `@prefix owl:` / `@prefix rdfs:` (ns_def_local); the draft's unused `@prefix rdf:` and `skos:` are dropped.

Context shim build.py (subset of src/util/build.py of d3fend/d3fend-ontology@cce593d61c): `get_graph`, `log`, `colors`, `PUBLIC_ONTOLOGY_FILEPATH` verbatim. FINDING OF THE CORPUS, not of the language: `_xmlns` is imported by update_atlas.py (and update_attack.py, test_cases.py) but build.py does not define it at that commit, so the real script raises ImportError; the shim restores it as the D3FEND namespace `http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#` (the one update_atlas.py binds as `d3fend`), used as `URIRef(_XMLNS + atlas_id)`. The local build.py shadows the PyPA `build` package installed in the venv (the driver runs with the example directory first on sys.path).

Fixture and calls (17): not deprecated (annotations added, returns 1), deprecated true / false (0), id absent as a literal, id present only as @en or ^^xsd:token (0: plain Literal() does not match), the id shared by a deprecated and a non-deprecated subject, a near-miss property (d3f:deprecated), an unknown technique, a non-string and a non-ASCII revoked_by, first mitre-atlas reference among several, and three techniques with no usable atlas id (`_XMLNS + None` -> TypeError, compared as a raise). The mutated graph argument is compared by isomorphism. Mutation check: `owl:deprecated` -> `rdfs:comment` in the read made `rdfeval check` FAIL; restored. (`{atlas_id}` without `Literal()` also passes: for a str the coercion gives the same plain literal; `Literal()` kept to stay faithful.)
optimization_notes: optimized.py: `tech = tech["data"]` is folded into the generator's iterable; the next() call takes two lines; the two nested ifs merge into one `and` (same short-circuit); `graph.value(atlas_uri, owl.deprecated) is None` becomes `(atlas_uri, owl.deprecated, None) not in graph` (value() returns None exactly when no object exists, so the falsy `owl:deprecated false` still counts as present); the `new` flag gives way to `return 1` / `return 0`; the three adds become one `graph += [...]`.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph graph`; the two existence tests are `m{ ?s ?p {atlas_id} } and not m{ {atlas_uri} owl:deprecated ?v }`; the three triples are one `+{ {atlas_uri} rdfs:seeAlso {Literal(revoked_by)} ; owl:deprecated true ; rdfs:comment f"This technique has been revoked by {revoked_by}" }`.

`{atlas_id}` drops translated.ldpy's `Literal()`: when the test is reached atlas_id is a str (`_XMLNS + atlas_id` has already raised TypeError on None or a number), and coercing a str gives the same plain literal. `{Literal(revoked_by)}` keeps its `Literal()`: the coercion differs from Literal() on None (TypeError instead of Literal('None'), and a JSON null is possible) and on URIRef/BNode. The comment is an f-string literal written in the island, the same value as Literal(f"...").
Rule 4 was measured on each part: the island forms are shorter here (130 tokens; with the Python existence tests 147, with the Python adds 158).
No exception to the symmetry: the change to an existence test is in both files.
header_optimization_notes: Python: RDF, RDFS, BNode, SKOS and the shim's get_graph go; Literal, Namespace, URIRef and _xmlns as _XMLNS stay, and so do the owl/rdfs Namespace lines.
LD Python: the same, and Namespace goes too (owl: and rdfs: are @prefix lines, both used).
